newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot LPGs mixed, players await EIA data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot LPGs mixed, players await EIA data.

text.p: U.S. spot LPG prices were mixed in quiet midday trade on Thursday as players await government inventory data to be released later this afternoon.
As of today, the Energy Information Administration report is now to be released weekly for the winter season, instead of every month as during the summer.

Few traders, however, could predict which way propane stocks will lie, but analyst Dan Lippe of Purvin & Gertz said he expects the U.S. Gulf Coast and the Midwest to show either a draw or remain flat.
"There still has been a lot of buying activity," by retailers and ethylene producers who are putting the product into secondary storage, said Lippe.
Secondary storage is not counted by the EIA.
"A draw should not be a cause of concern if it is understood where the product is going," added Lippe.
In Mont Belvieu, spot propane rose a quarter cent to between 49.50 cents and 49.75 cents a gallon with 49.75 cents traded, players said.
Conway, Kansas, hub spot material fell a quarter cent to 48.50/49.00 cents, traders said.
-- Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631
